# Bully

<!-- badges: start -->
<!-- badges: end -->

Try to guess the word, that our Bully the computer has picked from its only slightly biased,
 but very large word bank. 
     
The catch is that for every wrong guess you will be taunted.

 There's an escape entry to free up your console but you will leave with out dignity either.

 This is a package where the snark runs deep, each functions name reveals what Bully is really thinking.

## Installation

You can install the development version of bully like after it pushes to github

``` r
# FILL THIS IN! HOW CAN PEOPLE INSTALL YOUR DEV PACKAGE?
```

## Usage
You can begin your word guessing match against Bully by typing Bully().  
He might question your life choices, but he will proceed to run the game using helper functions.

The main parameter you can change is in Bully(), this controls the number of guesses per degree of patience bully loops through. 

If you explore the documentation you will find parameters to his helper functions which allow customization of the game including substituting your own vector of words for Bully to choose from in box_of_crayons(), or adjusting his responses.  These parameters are available in the documentation of the responsible functions. 

Fair warning, Bully insists on his dramatic entrance so the introductory function Oh_Hello is not easiliy customizable. 

It's important to note Bully will invoke his God of computers and ask for Mercy but still permit more than 7 guesses per loop. 

If you sign yourself up for more guessing and taunting than you bargained for you can escape by typing  "colonel_runaway" into your console, it will trigger an error in the function messy_human() returning your console to you. 

Good luck, and remember... Don't Blink. 

You'll still need to render `README.Rmd` regularly, to keep `README.md` up-to-date. `devtools::build_readme()` is handy for this.
